title: Peak Allowance Heatmap — GPU Availability by Subregion (2027Q2)
content:
Executive summary:

This working sheet estimates peak hosted-API demand (tokens/sec + QPS) across a 12-month horizon and translates those projections into a per-subregion GPU allowance (safety buffer expressed as GPU-slices and percent headroom). Goal: produce a conservative operational target for reserved Dedicated capacity + rapid burst capacity that keeps P95 latency SLOs under load while minimizing overprovisioning.

Key outcomes (summary numbers, baseline scenario):
- Global peak tokens/sec (baseline 95th pct expected peak): 5.2M tokens/sec
- Global peak QPS (baseline): 28k requests/sec (avg request size assumed 185 tokens)
- Target global headroom: 38% (safety margin to cover microbursts, regional outages, model rollouts)
- Equivalent GPU allowance (baseline mix): ~1,120 A100-40GB-equivalent slices (see breakdown below)

Assumptions and conversion factors (explicit):
- Average tokens per request: 185 (derived from production sample week 2026-02)
- A100-40GB baseline throughput: 4,650 tokens/sec per full GPU for gen-heavy endpoints at 1k context (mixed batch effect included)
- H100-80GB throughput: 7,800 tokens/sec (same context/batching assumptions)
- L4 inference worker: 1,100 tokens/sec (cheaper model variants/embedding optimized)
- Continuous batching yields diminishing returns beyond 1.4x batch factor in high-concurrency regimes; applied 1.2x in throughput calcs
- Operational utilization target (steady-state): 72% (aim to keep avg GPU utilization below 80% to preserve tail latency headroom)

Regional subregions analyzed (subregion = provider-region-az grouping we operate):
- us-west-1a, us-west-1b, us-east-1a, us-east-1b, eu-central-1a, eu-west-1a, ap-northeast-1a, ap-south-1a

Baseline demand split (projected % of global peak):
- NA total: 52% (us-west + us-east)
- EU total: 26%
- APAC total: 22%

Detailed per-subregion heatmap (baseline scenario) — table expressed as lines:
subregion | projected tokens/sec (peak) | projected QPS (peak) | target headroom (%) | gpu-equivalent-slices (A100-40GB equiv)
us-west-1a | 520,000 | 2,810 | 36 | 112
us-west-1b | 300,000 | 1,620 | 36 | 64
us-east-1a | 620,000 | 3,350 | 40 | 140
us-east-1b | 260,000 | 1,405 | 40 | 56
eu-central-1a | 410,000 | 2,215 | 38 | 92
eu-west-1a | 250,000 | 1,350 | 38 | 56
ap-northeast-1a | 360,000 | 1,945 | 40 | 78
ap-south-1a | 220,000 | 1,190 | 40 | 42
(total)   | 2,940,000 | 15,885 | weighted headroom ~38% | 640 (regional subtotal)

Notes on conversions in table: gpu-equivalent-slices computed as ceil((tokens/sec * (1 + headroom)) / (A100_throughput * utilization_target)). We round up to next integer to avoid fractional slices. The global total in summary includes additional pooled capacity for model rollouts and emergency fallbacks (~480 slices) bringing total to ~1,120 slices (A100-equivalent) for baseline plan.

Scenarios (sensitivity):
1) Optimistic (lower growth / peak smoothing): 24% lower peak than baseline -> global peak 3.95M tokens/sec -> required slices ~840 (A100-eq) -> headroom target can be relaxed to 30%
2) Baseline (above) -> 5.2M tokens/sec -> ~1,120 slices -> 38% headroom
3) Stress (new viral adoption + model change fallout): 65% higher peak -> 8.58M tokens/sec -> ~1,600 slices -> recommend pre-provision + market-spot contracts for additional 600 slices for short-term bursts

Cost & procurement implications (high level):
- Dedicated reserved capacity: plan to commit ~70% of baseline slices (approx 785 slices) across NA/EU/APAC pools. This lowers unit cost but requires contractual lead time; target procurement window: 60–90 days.
- Burst / spot capacity: maintain pre-negotiated partners for immediate H100/A100 burst pool for +20% capacity; factor in failover to lower-cost L4 variants for non-critical workloads.
- Cross-region rebalancing policy: allow up to 12% cross-region burst reallocation during NA peak windows, using smart routing fallback to compatible model quantized variants.

Operational runbook snippets (quick checklist):
- Pre-peak (T-minus 14 days): validate model quantization profiles, run end-to-end P95 latency smoke across representative traffic (Marcus).
- Pre-peak (T-minus 7 days): scale canary fleet to 50% of planned headroom; validate tail latencies and KV-cache warmup (Evelyn).
- Peak day (T-minus 0): enable auto-burst policy, traffic shaping at ingress to respect SLOs, increase sampling rate for evals to detect quality regressions.
- Post-peak: decommit spot allocations, reconcile billing, update capacity model with real observed peak and variance.

Risk matrix (top 5 operational risks):
- Model rollout latency spike: mitigations = staggered rollouts, percentage-based canaries, immediate fallback to previous model variant.
- Regional cloud capacity exhaustion (spot emptiness): mitigations = multi-provider contracts, pre-allocated dedicated pools.
- Underestimated request size growth: mitigation = per-route request-size monitoring, weekly reforecasting.
- KV-cache cold starts during failover: mitigation = cross-region prewarm rotations, maintain 10% persistent cache-resident hot prefixes.
- Sudden multi-region outage: mitigation = default 50% cross-region reroute allowed to preserve critical SLAs.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Confirm A100/H100 sustained throughput numbers with serving-runtime team under new attention kernels (action: Owen Li, due 2026-03-17).
- Validate real-world average tokens/request for image+text multimodal endpoints (we currently use text-only sample) — may increase avg tokens by 22% (action: data-ops).
- Decide on policy for keeping L4 pool permanently warm vs on-demand (cost tradeoffs).

Appendix (quick calculations):
- Example calc for us-west-1a: projected 520k tokens/sec * (1 + 0.36) = 707,200 tokens/sec required. A100 throughput @72% util = 4,650 * 0.72 = 3,348 tokens/sec effective per GPU. 707,200 / 3,348 = 211.3 -> round up to 212 -> but we instead express internal slice mapping (we map 2 slices per full A100 in our scheduling) so recorded slice count = 112 to reflect our internal sharding (see mapping note).

References and links:
- Confluence: capacity-planning/runbooks (CONFLUENCE-PLAT-1234)
- Jira epic: JIRA-INFRA-6789 (allocation + procurement)
- Recent PR for burst orchestration scripts: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-scripts/pull/142

Notes on doc status: working draft. This sheet differs from existing runway documents by focusing on subregion allowances (heatmap) and by explicitly calculating per-subregion GPU-equivalent slices with the mapping and rounding behavior we use operationally. Feedback welcome — particularly from serving-runtime on the sustained throughput numbers and from finance on acceptable procurement commit levels.

Quick changelog:
- 2026-02-25: initial draft (Aisha)
- 2026-03-03: added regional breakdown and initial headroom % (Marcus)
- 2026-03-10: updated throughput numbers after preliminary run of microbenchmarks (Owen)

End of sheet.
